expect.closures: UPDATED: The Bear Gulch Fire started July 6, 2025 (not September) near Lake Cushman and burned into the Staircase area. As of July 8, 2026 the Staircase developed area, FS-24 access road, campground, and ranger station have reopened. The actual approach to The Fin remains closed, however: the North Fork Skokomish River Trail is closed from its junction with the Staircase Rapids Loop to Home Sweet Home, and the Flapjack Lakes Trail is closed outright while crews complete hazard-tree removal and backcountry trail rehab, with no announced reopening date as of mid-2026. Check NPS 'Fire Conditions and Updates' before planning a trip.

value.fees: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/private vehicle (7 days), $15/individual on foot or bike, $55 annual park pass. The park does not accept cash — card only.
value.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
value.rules: Bear canisters mandatory for all food and scented items at Flapjack Lakes; no campfires above 3,500'; no stock/pack animals on this trail; bury human waste 6-8" deep and 200'+ from water where no toilet is available; Leave No Trace.
value.permit: Wilderness camping permit required for any overnight stay — reserve via recreation.gov ($6 reservation fee plus $8/person/night). Flapjack Lakes is a small, reservation-limited designated camping zone; no camping off-site. Groups of 7+ must use the designated group site.
value.closures: The Bear Gulch Fire started July 6, 2025 near Lake Cushman and burned into the Staircase area. On July 8, 2026 the Staircase developed area, FS-24 access road, campground, and ranger station reopened. The actual approach to The Fin remains closed, however: the North Fork Skokomish River Trail is closed from its junction with the Staircase Rapids Loop to Home Sweet Home, and the Flapjack Lakes Trail is closed outright while crews complete hazard-tree removal and backcountry trail rehab, with no end date given as of the Olympic National Park fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026. Check NPS 'Fire Conditions and Updates' before planning a trip.

expect.fees: Olympic NP entrance: $30/vehicle (7-day) or $15/person on foot/bike; $55 park annual pass. Overnight wilderness permit: $8/adult/night plus a $6 non-refundable reservation fee, or cover the nightly fee with a $45 annual NP Wilderness Pass.
expect.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
expect.rules: No campfires at Flapjack Lakes. Camp only in established sites or on durable/bare ground, at least 200 ft from water sources.
expect.permit: Wilderness permit required for any overnight stay, reserved via Recreation.gov / the Olympic NP Wilderness Information Center (360-565-3100). Flapjack Lakes is a limited-entry, quota-managed camping zone — reserve well in advance for summer weekends.
expect.closures: As of July 2026, the Staircase developed area and FS-24 access road have reopened following the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire closure. However, the North Fork Skokomish Trail beyond the Rapids Loop and the Flapjack Lakes Trail/campsite — the only practical approach to The Horn — remain closed while NPS crews complete hazard assessments and repair fire-damaged infrastructure (bridges, privies). Confirm current trail status with Olympic National Park before planning any trip.

expect.name: I-90 exit 143 to Silica Road SW and Vantage Road SW
expect.status: Paved the whole way. Vantage Road SW has been closed west of Silica Road SW since a May 2026 rockslide left an unstable rock face above it, with no reopening date announced; this cuts off the drive into Frenchman Coulee.
expect.driveNote: From I-90 take exit 143, turn left at the bottom of the ramp onto Silica Road SW and pass under the freeway, then take the first left onto Vantage Road SW and follow it down into the coulee to the main climbers' parking lot. A Discover Pass is required to park.
